label: Morning Brief
timezoneNote: All times shown in ET (America/New_York). Items marked headline were written only from the publisher's headline and summary. The overnight news snapshot for this morning was not available for this run, so coverage runs through about 8:56 PM ET on Nov 18.

driver.text: Per WSJ, US stocks ended mixed on Wednesday ahead of Anthropic's IPO, with Nvidia down again as its efforts to end questions around Jensen Huang's exit failed to stabilize the stock (5:14 PM ET). Per WSJ, the dollar rose to new 52-week highs after the minutes of the Federal Reserve's October meeting revealed mounting inflation concerns (5:59 PM ET). Per Bloomberg, gold rose from a 14-month low as dip buyers offset expectations the Fed will hike rates (6:24 PM ET). Per MarketWatch, Palo Alto Networks raised its outlook on earnings (8:02 PM ET). Written from headlines and publisher summaries only.

calendar.text: World leaders gather in Shenzhen for the APEC plenary, and Trump and Xi hold talks, per SCMP and Bloomberg.
The Federal Reserve published the minutes of the October 27-28 FOMC meeting.

items.headline: Alibaba's AI Ambitions Face Steep Challenge in US Chip Controls
items.summary: Per Bloomberg, Alibaba is facing mounting pressure to show it can deliver on its AI business plan despite new limits on its access to data center chips. Written from the headline and the publisher's summary only.

items.headline: Nvidia's Outlook Cut to Stable by Moody's on Governance Concerns
items.summary: Per Bloomberg, Moody's lowered Nvidia's credit-rating outlook to stable from positive, citing governance concerns following the ouster of longtime CEO Jensen Huang. Written from the headline and the publisher's summary only.

items.headline: Nvidia Says It's 'Business as Usual' After Huang's Ouster. Wall Street Doesn't Buy It.
items.summary: Per WSJ, Nvidia shares fell for a fifth straight session after its earnings call fell flat. Written from the headline and the publisher's summary only.

items.headline: Trump Hails 'Great' Ties With Xi, Downplays Nvidia Spy Scandal
items.summary: Per Bloomberg, President Trump hailed his 'friendship' with Chinese leader Xi Jinping and downplayed a spying scandal involving Nvidia, hours before the two leaders meet for talks in China. Written from the headline and the publisher's summary only.

items.headline: Nvidia's booming demand is 'hard to ignore,' but these four questions loom over the stock
items.summary: Per MarketWatch, Nvidia investors face uncertainty around CEO succession, the AI ecosystem, export controls and China. Written from the headline and the publisher's summary only.
